identity_policy.destination: slug plus external_id; numeric Django IDs are snapshot-local and must never merge separate databases
identity_policy.related_records: foreign keys are valid only inside this matched JSON/database pair

policy.destinations: active, approved, non-user-submitted, sourced records with valid Nepal coordinates
policy.images: approved external images with destination_match_score >= 0.85 and authenticity_score >= 0.85; AI/user uploads excluded
policy.privacy: users, tokens, sessions, logs, bookings, feedback, drafts, and local media paths excluded
policy.services: only explicitly verified hotels, restaurants, hospitals, police, and essential services

fields.description: Kathmandu District, in Bagmati Province, is the capital district of Nepal and the core of the Kathmandu Valley. It is home to the UNESCO World Heritage sites of Kathmandu Durbar Square, Swayambhunath, Pashupatinath and Boudhanath.
fields.name: Kathmandu

fields.description: Bhaktapur District occupies the eastern Kathmandu Valley in Bagmati Province. Its seat, Bhaktapur city, is a preserved medieval Newar city known for Bhaktapur Durbar Square, the Nyatapola temple and a living pottery tradition.
fields.name: Bhaktapur

fields.description: Lalitpur District lies immediately south of Kathmandu in Bagmati Province, centred on the old Newar city of Patan (Lalitpur). Patan Durbar Square is part of the UNESCO-inscribed Kathmandu Valley monument zone, and the district is renowned for Newar metalwork and craftsmanship.
fields.name: Lalitpur

fields.description: Chitwan District covers the south-western corner of Bagmati Province in the Terai lowlands, with Bharatpur as its administrative centre. It hosts Chitwan National Park, Nepal's first national park and a UNESCO World Heritage site, and is known for Tharu culture.
fields.name: Chitwan

fields.description: Rasuwa District in northern Bagmati Province covers the Langtang valley within Langtang National Park and the sacred Gosainkunda lakes, and reaches the Tibetan border at Rasuwagadhi.
fields.name: Rasuwa

fields.description: Kavrepalanchok District on the Kathmandu Valley rim in Bagmati Province is known for the viewpoint town of Dhulikhel and the Namobuddha monastery, both a short drive from the capital.
fields.name: Kavrepalanchok

fields.description: Sindhupalchok District in Bagmati Province stretches from the outskirts of Kathmandu to the Tibetan border and contains part of Langtang National Park, with Chautara as its seat. The district was near the epicentre of the 2015 Gorkha earthquake.
fields.name: Sindhupalchok

fields.description: Makwanpur District in Bagmati Province lies south of the Kathmandu Valley across the Chure hills, with Hetauda as its seat and the capital of Bagmati Province. The historic Makwanpur Gadhi fort sits above the district's main valley.
fields.name: Makwanpur

fields.description: Nuwakot District in Bagmati Province guards the historic Kathmandu–Tibet trade route at the Trishuli–Tadi river confluence, where the hilltop Nuwakot Durbar palace complex still stands.
fields.name: Nuwakot

fields.description: Dhading District in Bagmati Province stretches from the Trishuli corridor on the Prithvi Highway into the Ganesh Himal and Langtang foothills, serving as a western gateway to Langtang treks.
fields.name: Dhading

fields.description: Kaski District in Gandaki Province is centred on Pokhara, Nepal's second-largest city. Phewa Lake, Sarangkot and the district's position as the trailhead for the Annapurna trekking region make it one of the country's most-visited districts.
fields.name: Kaski

fields.description: Mustang District in Gandaki Province lies in the rain shadow of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges along the Kali Gandaki valley, with Jomsom as its seat. Upper Mustang, with the walled town of Lo Manthang, and the pilgrimage site of Muktinath are its best-known landmarks.
fields.name: Mustang

fields.description: Manang District in Gandaki Province is a high trans-Himalayan district on the Annapurna Circuit, home to Tilicho Lake — among the highest lakes in the world — below the Annapurna massif.
fields.name: Manang

fields.description: Tanahun District in Gandaki Province sits along the Prithvi Highway between Kathmandu and Pokhara, with Damauli (Vyasa) as its seat. It is known for the preserved hill town of Bandipur.
fields.name: Tanahun

fields.description: Gorkha District in Gandaki Province is the ancestral home of the Shah dynasty, whose hilltop Gorkha Durbar palace overlooks the town. Mount Manaslu, the world's eighth-highest mountain, rises in the district's north.
fields.name: Gorkha

fields.description: Lamjung District in Gandaki Province was a Himalayan kingdom whose hilltop Lamjung Durbar still stands; Besisahar, the traditional start of the Annapurna Circuit, and the Gurung village of Ghalegaun lie here.
fields.name: Lamjung

fields.description: Myagdi District in Gandaki Province lies beneath the Dhaulagiri massif along the Kali Gandaki valley, with Beni as its seat and the lowland gateway to Mustang.
fields.name: Myagdi

fields.description: Parbat, one of Nepal's smallest districts, sits in the Kali Gandaki gorge of Gandaki Province with Kushma as its seat — once the seat of the Parbat kingdom.
fields.name: Parbat

fields.description: Syangja is a hill district of Gandaki Province on the Siddhartha Highway between Butwal and Pokhara, known for its oranges and for paragliding from Sirkot. Recorded on this platform: the Sirkot paragliding hill and the Aandhikhola valley.
fields.name: Syangja

fields.description: Baglung District in Gandaki Province spans the middle Kali Gandaki valley, is known for its long suspension bridges, and reaches the Dhorpatan Hunting Reserve — Nepal's only hunting reserve — on the Dhaulagiri foothills.
fields.name: Baglung

fields.description: Solukhumbu District in Koshi Province contains Mount Everest (Sagarmatha) and the UNESCO-inscribed Sagarmatha National Park. The Khumbu valley, Namche Bazar and Lukla airstrip sit here, and the district is the homeland of the Sherpa people.
fields.name: Solukhumbu

fields.description: Ilam District in the far-eastern hills of Koshi Province is famous for its tea gardens on the Mechi-range slopes, with hilltop viewpoints such as Kanyam drawing visitors year-round.
fields.name: Ilam

fields.description: Jhapa is Nepal's easternmost Terai district (Koshi Province), known for its tea gardens and for Kakarbhitta, the busiest Nepal–India border crossing in the east.
fields.name: Jhapa

fields.description: Morang District in the south-eastern Terai of Koshi Province is centred on Biratnagar, the province capital and one of Nepal's largest industrial cities.
fields.name: Morang

fields.description: Sunsari District in the eastern Terai (Koshi Province) contains Dharan, the gateway city to the eastern hills, and part of the Koshi Tappu Wildlife Reserve, a Ramsar wetland famous for its bird life and wild water buffalo.
fields.name: Sunsari

fields.description: Taplejung District in north-eastern Koshi Province borders Mount Kanchenjunga, the world's third-highest mountain, within the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area. The Pathibhara Devi temple is a major pilgrimage site.
fields.name: Taplejung

fields.description: Sankhuwasabha District in Koshi Province contains Mount Makalu, the world's fifth-highest mountain, and most of Makalu Barun National Park in the remote eastern Himalaya.
fields.name: Sankhuwasabha

fields.description: Rupandehi District in Lumbini Province contains Lumbini, the birth place of the Buddha and a UNESCO World Heritage site. The district borders India and also includes the archaeological site of Tilaurakot (ancient Kapilavastu).
fields.name: Rupandehi

fields.description: Palpa District in the Lumbini hills is centred on the old Sen-dynasty town of Tansen, perched above the Siddhartha Highway, and on Rani Mahal, the riverside palace built on the Kali Gandaki in 1893.
fields.name: Palpa

fields.description: Kapilvastu is a Terai district of Lumbini Province named for the ancient Shakya-kingdom region, with Taulihawa as its seat. Recorded on this platform: Aurorakot and Dohani heritage sites, the Banganga river and Badki Mai temple.
fields.name: Kapilvastu

fields.description: Banke District in Lumbini Province is centred on Nepalgunj, the transport hub of western Nepal, and contains Banke National Park, part of the Terai Arc tiger conservation landscape.
fields.name: Banke

fields.description: Bardiya District in Lumbini Province contains Bardiya National Park, the largest national park of the Terai, along the Karnali river — prime wildlife country and a centre of Tharu culture.
fields.name: Bardiya

fields.description: Mugu District in remote north-western Karnali Province contains Rara Lake, Nepal's largest lake, protected within Rara National Park at about 2,990 m in the high Himalaya.
fields.name: Mugu

fields.description: Dolpa District in Karnali Province is Nepal's largest district by area, centred on Shey Phoksundo National Park and the turquoise Phoksundo Lake; its trans-Himalayan Upper Dolpo valleys are home to centuries-old monasteries such as Shey Gompa.
fields.name: Dolpa

fields.description: Jumla District in Karnali Province holds the Sinja valley, where the Khas language ancestral to modern Nepali is believed to have developed; the high-altitude town is famed for its sinja rice and marsi crops.
fields.name: Jumla

fields.description: Surkhet District is the gateway to Karnali Province, with the planned city of Birendranagar as its seat and the province capital. The Kakrebihar Buddhist monastery ruins lie nearby.
fields.name: Surkhet

fields.description: Dhanusha District in Madhesh Province is centred on Janakpurdham, the province capital. The Janaki Mandir temple, dedicated to Sita, makes the city a major Hindu pilgrimage site and a centre of Maithili culture.
fields.name: Dhanusha

fields.description: Parsa District in Madhesh Province is centred on Birgunj, one of Nepal's largest trade cities on the Indian border, and holds Parsa National Park along the Chure foothills.
fields.name: Parsa

fields.description: Kanchanpur District anchors the far-western Terai of Sudurpashchim Province and contains Shuklaphanta National Park, one of Nepal's largest grassland reserves, known for its swamp deer herds.
fields.name: Kanchanpur

fields.description: Kailali District occupies the western Terai of Sudurpashchim Province, with Godawari as its seat and the province capital. Ghodaghodi Lake, a Ramsar-listed wetland, lies in the district.
fields.name: Kailali

fields.description: Doti District in Sudurpashchim Province shares Khaptad National Park — alpine meadows and forests sacred to the Khaptad Baba — with Dipayal-Silgadhi as its seat on the Seti river.
fields.name: Doti

fields.description: Bhojpur is a hill district of Koshi Province along the Arun river, long famed for its khukuri blade-makers. Recorded on this platform: Bhojpur Bazaar and its craft and food trails.
fields.name: Bhojpur

fields.description: Dhankuta is a hill district of Koshi Province above the Mulghat gateway on the Koshi corridor. Recorded on this platform: the Bhedetar hill station and viewpoint, its waterfall, and the Bhanu Bhakta Memorial.
fields.name: Dhankuta

fields.description: Khotang is a hill district of Koshi Province whose Halesi Maratika cave temple — a major Shiva shrine also sacred to Buddhists — is the far-east's most visited pilgrimage site. Recorded on this platform: Halesi Mahadev and Barahapokhari.
fields.name: Khotang

fields.description: Okhaldhunga is a hill district of Koshi Province whose name comes from a legendary stone mortar (okhal), with Siddhicharan as its seat. Recorded on this platform: Okhaldhunga Bazaar and the surrounding hill villages.
fields.name: Okhaldhunga

fields.description: Panchthar is a hill district of Koshi Province in the Limbuwan heartland, with Phidim as its seat. Recorded on this platform: the Chiwabhanjyang Limbu heritage site, Aagejung monastery and Battise waterfall.
fields.name: Panchthar

fields.description: Terhathum is a hill district of Koshi Province with Myanglung as its seat. Recorded on this platform: Hyatung waterfall — among Nepal's tallest — and the Basantapur bazaar on the Tamor corridor.
fields.name: Terhathum

fields.description: Udayapur is an Inner Terai district of Koshi Province with Gaighat as its seat in the Udayapur valley. Recorded on this platform: the Chaudandigadhi fort and local Shiva shrines.
fields.name: Udayapur

fields.description: Bara District in the central Terai (Madhesh Province) contains the ruins of Simraungadh, the medieval capital of the Karnat dynasty, with Kalaiya as its seat.
fields.name: Bara

fields.description: Mahottari is a Terai district of Madhesh Province with Jaleshwar as its seat on the Indian border. Recorded on this platform: the Jaleshwar Mahadev and Aurahi Mahadev temples.
fields.name: Mahottari

fields.description: Rautahat is a Terai district of Madhesh Province with Gaur as its seat near the Indian border. Recorded on this platform: the Barahwa wetland and Brindaban forest.
fields.name: Rautahat

fields.description: Saptari District lies in the south-eastern Terai of Madhesh Province, with Rajbiraj — one of Nepal's earliest planned grid cities — as its seat.
fields.name: Saptari

fields.description: Sarlahi is a farm-rich Terai district of Madhesh Province with Malangwa as its seat. Recorded on this platform: the Chaturbhujeshwar temple and Malangwa's Buddha Park.
fields.name: Sarlahi

fields.description: Siraha is a Terai district of Madhesh Province along the Kamala river. Recorded on this platform: Salhesh Phulbari, a pilgrimage site of the Dusadh folk hero Salhesh, near Lahan.
fields.name: Siraha

fields.description: Dolakha District in Bagmati Province reaches from the hills east of Kathmandu to Mount Gaurishankar on the Tibetan border, with Bhimeshwor (Charikot) as its seat and the Kalinchok temple above the valley.
fields.name: Dolakha

fields.description: Ramechhap District in Bagmati Province is a gateway to the Everest region; flights to Lukla commonly depart from Manthali airport here, and the classic Jiri trek route passes through the district.
fields.name: Ramechhap

fields.description: Sindhuli District in Bagmati Province takes its name from Sindhuligadhi fort, where Nepali forces repelled a British column in 1767 — among the earliest victories of unification-era Nepal.
fields.name: Sindhuli

fields.description: Nawalpur is an Inner Terai district of Gandaki Province bordering Chitwan National Park's eastern buffer zone, with Kawasoti as its seat. Recorded on this platform: the Tharu homestay village of Amaltari and its jungle-edge lodges.
fields.name: Nawalpur

fields.description: Arghakhanchi is a hill district of Lumbini Province with Sandhikharka as its seat. Recorded on this platform: the Argha Durbar and Argali Darbar heritage sites and the Chhatradev Devalaya temple.
fields.name: Arghakhanchi

fields.description: Dang District in Lumbini Province spans the Dang and Deukhuri valleys and hosts the province's administrative seat at Deukhuri. Ghorahi and Tulsipur are its largest cities.
fields.name: Dang

fields.description: Eastern Rukum is a Himalayan district of Lumbini Province, formed in 2017 when Rukum was split in two, with Rukumkot as its seat beneath sacred Mount Sisne. Tourism places are still being recorded here.
fields.name: Rukum East

fields.description: Gulmi is a hill district of Lumbini Province with Tamghas as its seat and a growing reputation for coffee. Recorded on this platform: Gulmi coffee farms, the Chhahara waterfall and Bichitra Cave.
fields.name: Gulmi

fields.description: Parasi (Nawalparasi West) is a Terai district of Lumbini Province whose Ramgram Stupa is traditionally counted among the eight original stupas holding the Buddha's relics. Recorded on this platform: Ramgram, Balmiki Ashram and the district's river-side temples.
fields.name: Parasi

fields.description: Pyuthan is a hill district of Lumbini Province with Khalanga as its seat in the Jhimruk valley. Recorded on this platform: the Gaumukhi cave shrine and the Jhimruk river terraces.
fields.name: Pyuthan

fields.description: Rolpa is a hill district of Lumbini Province with Libang (Rolpa Bazar) as its seat — the heartland of Nepal's People's War, now crossed by the Guerrilla Trek. Recorded on this platform: the Guerrilla Trek and the villages of Holeri and Jelbang.
fields.name: Rolpa

fields.description: Dailekh is a hill district of Karnali Province whose Dullu valley holds the stone inscriptions of the medieval Khasa kingdom. Recorded on this platform: the Akhanda Jwala eternal flame, Basudhara temple and Badapokhara at Dullu.
fields.name: Dailekh

fields.description: Humla District in far north-western Karnali Province is among Nepal's most remote, with Simikot as its airhead; the Limi valley caravans historically linked it to the Mount Kailash pilgrimage route in Tibet.
fields.name: Humla

fields.description: Jajarkot is a hill district of Karnali Province with Khalanga as its seat. Recorded on this platform: the Barekot heritage trail, the chortens of Jajarkot and Ghalemdi waterfall.
fields.name: Jajarkot

fields.description: Kalikot is a hill district of Karnali Province with Manma as its seat. Recorded on this platform: the Dademasta and Bobka Than shrines, Chuli Malika peak and Bayal waterfall.
fields.name: Kalikot

fields.description: Salyan is a hill district of Karnali Province with Salyan Khalanga as its seat. Recorded on this platform: the Chhayakshetra and Khairabang pilgrimage temples and Kachuwa Daha lake.
fields.name: Salyan

fields.description: Western Rukum is a Himalayan district of Karnali Province, formed in 2017 when Rukum was split in two, with Musikot as its seat in the Bheri river valley. Tourism places are still being recorded here.
fields.name: Rukum West

fields.description: Achham is a hill district of Sudurpashchim Province with Mangalsen as its seat. Recorded on this platform: the Baidyanath Dham temple complex and the historic sites of Bannigadhi and Jayagadh.
fields.name: Achham

fields.description: Baitadi is a hill district of Sudurpashchim Province with Dasharathchand as its seat. Recorded on this platform: the Deulek Kedar temple and Baitadi's waterfalls.
fields.name: Baitadi

fields.description: Bajhang is a Himalayan district of Sudurpashchim Province with Chainpur as its seat, on the western approaches to Khaptad. Recorded on this platform: the Bajhang Tatopani hot springs and the temples of Bithadchir.
fields.name: Bajhang

fields.description: Bajura is a Himalayan district of Sudurpashchim Province whose hilltop Badimalika shrine is one of the far-west's great pilgrimage sites. Recorded on this platform: Badimalika Dham and the Budhiganga river valley.
fields.name: Bajura

fields.description: Dadeldhura is a hill district of Sudurpashchim Province named for the Amargadhi fort that crowns its seat town. Recorded on this platform: Amargadhi, the Ajayameru Kot ruins and Aalital Lake.
fields.name: Dadeldhura

fields.description: Darchula is Nepal's westernmost district (Sudurpashchim Province), bordering both India and China beneath Api, the 7,161 m peak of the Gurans Himal; its Byans valley preserves ancient trans-border trade traditions.
fields.name: Darchula

fields.name: Tilaurakot

fields.name: Nigalihawa

fields.description: Gotihawa (ancient Khemavati) is a village in Kapilvastu District regarded as the birthplace of Kakusandha Buddha. The base of an Ashokan pillar (protected monument NP-KP-04) was discovered here, 4 km southeast of Kapilvastu.
fields.name: Gotihawa

fields.description: Kupinde Daha is a pristine high-altitude lake in Salyan District, Karnali Province. The lake changes color according to season and is surrounded by lush green hills, pine trees, and the revered Barah Temple. It is a peaceful destination for boating, nature photography, and cultural pilgrimages.
fields.name: Kupinde Daha Lake
fields.short_description: Scenic mountain lake in Salyan surrounded by dense pine forests and sacred Barah shrine.

fields.description: Chhatreshwari Temple is a major Hindu pilgrimage site in Salyan. According to sacred scriptures, this is where Goddess Sati spine fell. Uniquely, animal sacrifices are strictly prohibited at this temple, and devotees offer flowers, belpatra, and sacred milk.
fields.name: Chhatreshwari Shakti Peeth
fields.short_description: Sacred Shakti Peeth temple on a hill ridge in Salyan venerated across Karnali.

fields.description: Luham Valley lies along the banks of the clear Sharada River in Salyan. Famous for its terraced organic ginger farms, citrus orchards, and mountain honey production, it offers scenic riverside walks and authentic rural village hospitality.
fields.name: Sharada River & Luham Valley
fields.short_description: Fertile agricultural valley along Sharada River famous for organic ginger and mountain honey.

fields.description: Ramgram Stupa is a ancient brick stupa located in Parasi (Nawalparasi West). It is the only stupa containing unopened original corporeal relics (Dhatu) of Lord Buddha, protected historically by a king cobra (Naga) and wild elephants under a grand Banyan tree.
fields.name: Ramgram Sacred Relic Stupa
fields.short_description: UNESCO tentative list site containing the only untouched corporal relics of Lord Buddha.

fields.description: Triveni Dham is a sacred river confluence in Parasi at the junction of three rivers. It is surrounded by historic temples, Valmiki Ashram from Ramayana epic, and hosting the grand Maghe Sankranti Mela festival every winter.
fields.name: Triveni Dham Confluence
fields.short_description: Holy confluence of Narayani, Sona, and Tamasa rivers near Valmiki Ashram.

fields.description: Jaleshwarnath Temple in Jaleshwar, Mahottari, is a revered pilgrimage site where the main Shiva Lingam resides in an underground cave continuously submerged under natural spring water. Devotees visit during Shivaratri and Shrawan month to perform holy Jalabhishek.
fields.name: Jaleshwarnath Mahadev Temple
fields.short_description: Historic submerged Shiva lingam temple immersed in natural underground spring water.

fields.description: Located in Mahottari District, Pipara Mithila Cultural Center celebrates centuries of Maithili folk art, wall paintings, clay pottery, and traditional music. Visitors can observe local women artists hand-painting Mithila artwork on natural handmade paper.
fields.name: Mithila Cultural Heritage Hub
fields.short_description: Artisan center for traditional Mithila folk painting, terracotta pottery, and Maithili crafts.

fields.description: Jaljala in Rolpa is a breathtaking alpine wetland plateau at 3,100m elevation. It features the sacred Gorakhnath Temple, rhododendron forests, and unobstructed views of Mt. Dhaulagiri, Mt. Kanjirowa, and Mt. Sisne.
fields.name: Gorakhnath Temple & Jaljala Ridge
fields.short_description: High alpine grassland plateau at 3,100m offering sweeping vistas of Dhaulagiri and Sisne peaks.

fields.description: The Guerilla Trek passes through Thawang and the scenic heartland of Rolpa. It offers a unique cultural trek through remote Kham Magar indigenous villages, traditional slate-roofed houses, organic terraced farming, and wilderness river canyons.
fields.name: Guerilla Trek Heritage Trail
fields.short_description: Historic trekking route through authentic Magar ethnic villages and pine forest gorges.

fields.description: Syarpu Lake (Syarpu Taal) is a freshwater lake located in Rukum West, Karnali Province. Spanning over 2.6 sq km, the lake is ideal for boating, fish tasting, and village homestays amidst terraced hills.
fields.name: Syarpu Lake & Resort
fields.short_description: Pristine mountain lake in Rukum West surrounded by terraced hills and local homestays.

fields.description: Musikot viewpoint in Rukum West provides a dramatic vantage point facing Mt. Sisne (5,849m), the iconic virgin horn peak of Karnali. The area features pine forests, historic hill forts, and panoramic mountain sunrises.
fields.name: Sisne Himal Viewpoint
fields.short_description: Majestic viewpoint facing the sacred unclimbed pyramid peak of Mt. Sisne (5,849m).

fields.description: Dhanushadham is a historic pilgrimage forest 18 km from Janakpur. According to Ramayana, a piece of Shiva bow fell here when Lord Ram broke it during Sita Swayamvar. The site features a petrified bow fossil shrine surrounded by a protected forest sanctuary.
fields.name: Dhanushadham Sacred Forest
fields.short_description: Mythological forest site where Shiva divine bow fell during Sita Swayamvar in Ramayana.

fields.description: Badimalika in Bajura is one of Sudurpashchim most sacred mountain shrines, located atop rolling alpine meadows at 4,200m elevation. Devotees undertake a 3-day scenic trek through wildflower grasslands to worship Goddess Bhagwati during Janai Purnima.
fields.name: Badimalika Sacred Meadows
fields.short_description: High alpine grassland shrine at 4,200m offering 360-degree Himalayan vistas.

fields.description: Salhesh Fulbari in Siraha is a sacred historical garden associated with the ancient folk hero King Salhesh. Uniquely, rare Haram orchid flowers bloom on a specific tree in this garden only on Chaitra 31st (Nepali New Year Eve) and fade by the end of Baisakh 1st.
fields.name: Salhesh Fulbari Miracle Garden
fields.short_description: Historical garden famous for the miracle blooming of orchids every Nepali New Year Eve.

fields.description: Halesi Mahadev Cave in Khotang is a natural limestone cave complex known as the Maratika Cave in Tibetan Buddhism and Pashupatinath of East Nepal. It is venerated as the place where Lord Shiva hid from demon Bhasmasur and Padmasambhava attained immortal life.
fields.name: Halesi Mahadev Limestone Cave
fields.short_description: Pashupatinath of East Nepal sacred natural cave venerated by Hindus, Buddhists, and Kirats.
